note: Techniques shown in the Motion DNA panel (Techniques). Each one is a script workflow, not a single preset: what it does, how to run it by hand, and what to ask Claude (MCP server motion-dna). "tool": the MCP tool that runs it, when there is one.

techniques.name: Tracked labels
techniques.what: Labels, callouts and brackets that stick to moving details in footage (shoes, faces, products).
techniques.how: python tools/track_points.py clip.mp4 --regions regions.json -o tracks.json, then a scene JSON with HUD items built by tools/build_scene.jsx (SSHUD.callout / bracket / chip on TRK nulls).
techniques.ask: Track the car in this shot and add an AEROSPACE EXTERIOR label that follows it.

techniques.name: Text behind people
techniques.what: Big type that sits behind the subject, cut by an AI matte.
techniques.how: Get a person matte (VEED background removal or rembg), then a scene JSON with "matte" and "behind" text (tools/build_scene.jsx).
techniques.ask: Put a giant YES! behind the two people cheering in this shot.

techniques.name: Roto breakdown
techniques.what: A 2×2 grid that shows plate, matte, contours and the final composite.
techniques.ask: Make a roto breakdown of the YES shot: plate, matte, contour and composite.

techniques.name: HUD overlays
techniques.what: Holographic scans, meters, chips and face scans on tracked points.
techniques.how: #include tools/ss_hud.jsx · SSHUD.bracket / callout / meter / chip / contour / faceScan on TRK nulls.
techniques.ask: Add command chips that float around the robot's screen in this shot.

techniques.name: Speed ramps
techniques.what: Slow-mo → burst → slow-mo on footage, on the Ramp, Surge or Whip curve, with frame blending.
techniques.how: Moves > Speed Ramp on a footage layer or precomp, or "speed" segments in an edit JSON (tools/build_edit.jsx).
techniques.ask: Speed-ramp the car's lift-off: slow-mo as it leaves the ground, then fast out, with the Ramp curve and a whoosh.

techniques.name: Freeze frame + kinetic type
techniques.what: The shot freezes, the subject is cut out and big words slam in around it.
techniques.how: "freeze" in an edit JSON (tools/build_edit.jsx): heroWord, leadWord, plate cut-out, SFX.
techniques.ask: Freeze on Dana's close-up and slam in EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. beside her face.

techniques.name: Shape-wipe transitions
techniques.what: Two-colour bars that travel through a cut in one continuous move.
techniques.how: "wipe" elements (mode out at the end of a scene, mode in at the start of the next, same colours and direction) in a promo spec (tools/build_explainer.jsx).
techniques.ask: Join the office scene and the car spot with a Spark and Sea wipe.

techniques.name: Marker timing
techniques.what: Drag the SS in / SS out layer markers to retime an animation; the curve keeps its shape.
techniques.how: Tick Marker timing in Controls before applying (or SSP.markerTiming(true) in a script).
techniques.ask: Apply Surge Rise with marker timing to Rex's Make it pop title, so I can retime it by dragging SS in and SS out.

techniques.name: Styles
techniques.what: One click gives a whole comp a look: each layer gets the preset for its role (title, text, shape, media, logo).
techniques.how: Styles category, pick one, then In / Out / Both (SSP.applyPack).
techniques.ask: Apply the Dynamic style to this spot and show me a frame.

techniques.name: Cut on the voice
techniques.what: Scenes change only in the pauses of a voiceover; words land on the beats they are spoken.
techniques.how: python tools/vo_words.py vo.mp3 words.json, then cut times from the words (see media/promo/make_promo.py).
techniques.ask: Cut this edit to the voiceover word times and land MOVES. on Rex's word.

techniques.name: Face refinement
techniques.what: For clips with real people: puts their real face back on generated video, keeping wardrobe and camera.
techniques.how: media/faceswap/jobs.json + python tools/faceswap_refine.py (MiniMax H3, local GPU), then tools/faceswap_apply.py.
techniques.ask: Check Dana's face in the new clips against her reference sheet and refine it before we edit.

techniques.name: Stroke build
techniques.what: A filled logo or shape assembles piece by piece: it is split into its pieces (thick strands, thin lines, the arrow), each drawn by a stroke along its centre line (Trim Paths on token curves) under a matte of its own outline, while the edges dissolve into fine grain that settles clean as the last piece lands. Our end card closes every Motion DNA demo with it.
techniques.how: python tools/logo_to_shape.py logo_traced.svg assets/brand/<name> (clean curves), then python tools/logo_parts.py assets/brand/<name>.json (pieces + centre strokes); MCP add_element(kind="end_card", logo="assets/brand/<name>.json", text=…, sub=…, style="horizontal" for the side lockup) or SSE.endCard(comp, {logo, text, tagline, layout, grain}). Manual: Figma "Motion DNA — Logo & Library".
techniques.ask: Close the video on our logo: build the mark stroke by stroke, then MOTION / DNA rising under it.

techniques.name: Sound pass
techniques.what: Every finished animation gets its sound effects, made in code (Tone.js) so they are ours to ship: a whoosh on cuts and big moves, a swish on medium moves, a pop when something scales in, a soft tick when text arrives, and whatever a marker 'sfx: <name>' asks for. Each lands one frame after its picture, a repeated sound rotates takes, and it all arrives as one audio layer, Motion DNA sound.
techniques.how: MCP add_sound (auto: reads the comp through tools/sound_events.jsx; or cues [{t, sfx}]); tools/sound_kit.py renders the WAV in headless Chrome. Hear the kit: tools/sound/kit.html. Run it when the animation is final and again after retiming; real music goes in with add_asset.
techniques.ask: Give this comp its sound effects.
